items.description: Plan trips and build day-by-day travel itineraries, delivered as one polished, standalone HTML page. Use this skill PROACTIVELY for any travel-planning request — trigger on "帮我规划行程 / 旅游攻略 / X日游 / 安排去XX玩 / 做旅行计划 / 行程安排 / 帮我排个行程", on "plan a trip / make an itinerary / X-day trip to a city / things to do in a place", and whenever the user gives a destination plus dates or a duration (e.g. "6月去东京玩5天", "国庆想去成都4天", "trip to Kyoto next month", "下周末杭州两日游"). Always gather requirements first (never jump straight to an itinerary), research transport/weather/opening-hours via web search (query-only — it never books or pays), then output ONE self-contained HTML file with an embedded Leaflet + OpenStreetMap map, per-day timeline cards, transport-segment cards, a budget table, a pre-departure checklist, collapsible sections, hierarchical navigation, scroll-memory, and 注意/必订/避雷 callouts. Do NOT use for academic study notes (use study-notes) or generic business reports (use visual-report).

latestVersion.changelog:
Trip Planner skill initial release.

- Provides detailed, day-by-day travel itineraries as polished standalone HTML files with interactive maps.
- Proactively triggers for travel-planning queries, automatically gathering user requirements through structured interviews before planning.
- Rigorously verifies all facts (prices, times, reviews); no numbers or opinions are shown unless actually researched in-session, with strict source labeling.
- Integrates web search and DOM scraping for real data; never invents details or estimates where real values are required.
- Output includes timeline and transport cards, budget breakdown, pre-departure checklist, and visually organized, collapsible sections.
- Clear distinction between verified and placeholder data to maximize accuracy and trustworthiness.

latestVersion.changelog:
huangdi-neijing v1.0.0

- Initial release of the huangdi-neijing skill, providing key concepts and practical wisdom from China's earliest medical classic.
- Includes core principles: 天人相应 (Harmony of Man and Nature), 气论自然观 (Qi Theory), 阴阳五行 (Yin-Yang and Five Elements), 形神统一 (Unity of Body and Spirit), and 养生之道 (Way of Health Maintenance).
- Offers guidance for health preservation, lifestyle, seasonal adaptation, constitution differentiation, preventive health thinking, and balancing work-life.
- Features summaries on 四时养生 (seasonal health), 治未病 (disease prevention), 五态体质 (constitution types), 五味与健康 (dietary guidance), age-related health rhythms, and the vital role of Yang Qi.
- Provides analysis frameworks and consultation templates for practical application in daily wellness and self-care.
